To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of Bu/Cy/Mel conditioning regimen for pediatric AML patients is superior to the other two regimens (TBICy and Bu/Cy) in terms of relapse rate, LFS and OS.

the combination of busulfan/cyclophosphamide/melphalan is the best conditioning regimen for children and young adults undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem transplantation for acute myeloid leukaemia in first complete remision.

the use of a myeloablative conditioning with busulfan, cyclophosphamid and melphalan was associated with a reduced risk of relapse and improved leukemia free survival in children with high risk acute myeloid leukaemia in first complete remision undergoing allogeneic haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of different chemotherapy protocols for the treatment of children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL).
the impact of conditioning regimens in children with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) undergoing allogeneic haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (HSCT).
the use of a new drug, which can be used to prevent relapse in patients undergoing HSCT for the treatment of AML.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the conditioning regimen with busulfan, cyclophosphamid and melphalan seems to be superior to the conditioning regimen with total body irradiation and cyclophoshamide in pediatric patients with A.M.L. in first complete remisson.
the use of Bu/Cy/Flu conditioning in pediatric AML in CR is the preferred conditioning regimen, as it is associated with a lower relapse risk and a similar NRM as compared to Bu/Cy.
BuCyMel conditioning regimen has the best balance of relapse, NRM, and survival in children with AML in CR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in children and young adults with AML in CR, BuCyMel is associated with a reduced risk of relapse compared with BuCy, without a significant increase in the risk of NRM.
BuCyMel is superior to BuCy and TBI in terms of relapse and LFS.
BuCyMel conditioning is the most effective in terms of relapse prevention in children with AML undergoing allogeneic stem cell transplant in CR1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Bu-Cy-Mel conditioning regimen in children with AML in first remission is associated with a better disease control and survival.
the use of Bu, Cy and Mel as conditioning regimen for HSCT in pediatric patients with AAML is associated with improved LFS and OS compared with BuCy or TBICy.
the use of Bu, Cy, Mel as the conditioning regimen for children with AML in CR 1 is superior to Bu, Cy or TBICy in reducing relapse, and improving leukemia free survival.
